# 3.5. Difference between Simulation and Real World

Collecting training samples is not an easy task while solving the problem of controls in soft robotics as it is in perception for similar systems. Collection of the real-world dataset (state-action pair) is a costly operation due to the high dimensionality of the control spaces and the lack of availability of a central source of control data for every environment. This inflicts various challenges while bringing models that have been trained in simulation to real-world scenarios.

This transfer remains challenging because of the so-called sim-to-real gap [10]. This gap describes slight but important discrepancies between reality and simulation. One approach to close this gap is to extend the simulation with physical process models and thus improve its accuracy and enrich the generated data.
